subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift guards as a core durable run-state contract, and what artifact, timer, persistence, and flag semantics should that contract enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix chooses public runtime semantics, persistent state ownership, operator-visible escalation behavior, and configuration/feature-flag shape across core agent execution.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define a core contract for artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, and post-green closure before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Existing Lifecycle Work
options.body: Make this issue's acceptance criteria part of the broader atomic run lifecycle and structured process-events design to avoid competing state machines.

options.title: Keep Adjacent Safeguards Only
options.body: Treat current loop, liveness, and no-fake-progress mitigations as sufficient and close or narrow this issue to documentation and telemetry follow-up.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define a core contract for artifacts, phases, blockers, escalation cooldowns, and post-green closure before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the official code owner and has recent review/landing history on adjacent runtime reliability contract work.
